extracted.intended_audience: Users of the GAP system (computational group theorists, mathematicians, and programmers) working with character tables and class functions
extracted.subtask_description: Reference rules and behavioral specifications for creating, inspecting, manipulating, printing, restricting/inducing, and performing arithmetic on class function objects and related character-table operations in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class function object equality semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A class function object is equal to its values list in the sense of \= (31.11.1), so class function objects can be used wherever their values lists can be used, but there are operations for class function objects that do not work just with values lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class function objects behave like their values lists for equality/comparison, but certain class-function-specific operations (that rely on an underlying character table attribute) require the object form. Examples show class function objects printed as Character(...) or ClassFunction(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer returning class function objects from library functions
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP library functions prefer to return class function objects rather than returning just values lists (for example Irr lists consist of class function objects, and TrivialCharacter returns a class function object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing or using GAP library routines, expect and prefer class function objects; using plain lists may require supplying additional table arguments to functions that expect class function objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingCharacterTable attribute presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Class function objects store the character table of the group G as value of the attribute UnderlyingCharacterTable (72.2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ordering of entries in the values list refers to the ordering of conjugacy classes in this underlying character table. Access to the group itself is only via the character table and only if the character table stores its group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering refers to character table, not group
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that if the character table has access to its underlying group then the ordering of conjugacy classes in the group and in the character table may differ; class functions always refer to the ordering of classes in the character table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when mixing class functions and group-based operations: class function indices correspond to table ordering. When converting between group-based data and table-based data ensure the fusion/ordering is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValuesOfClassFunction returns values list
rubrics_metrics.description: ValuesOfClassFunction(psi) is the list of values of the class function psi, the i-th entry being the value on the i-th conjugacy class of the underlying character table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ValuesOfClassFunction lets you obtain the raw list (and many list operations work). Examples demonstrate IsList, indexing, Length to inspect values. But some class-function-specific operations require the object form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class functions vs mappings design rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Class functions in GAP are represented as immutable lists (not as mappings) to distinguish characteristics and to ensure that the product of two class functions is again a class function (product defined as tensor product, not composition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design choice affects equality across characteristics (trivial characters in different characteristics are distinct objects) and arithmetic semantics: expect pointwise/tensor operations rather than mapping composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison semantics (=, <) mirror values lists
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to \= and \< (31.11.1), class functions behave equally to their lists of values: two class functions are equal iff their lists of values are equal, regardless of underlying table/group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality comparisons ignore whether the underlying tables differ; consequences shown in examples where irr1 = irr2 is true even for different tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic closure rules for sums and scalar multiples
rubrics_metrics.description: The scalar multiple of a class function with a cyclotomic is a class function; the sum and the difference of two class functions of the same underlying character table are again class functions of this table. The sum and the difference of a class function and a list that is not a class function are plain lists, as well as the sum and the difference of two class functions of different character tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining class functions, ensure they have the same underlying table to retain a class function result. Mixing types yields plain lists (losing class-function metadata). Examples illustrate 2 * irr[5] yields a Character, but irr[5] + [1,2,...] yields a plain list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicative behavior: tensor (pointwise) product
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of two class functions of the same character table is the tensor product (pointwise product) of these class functions; hence the set of all class functions of a fixed group forms a ring and the F-span forms an algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product of class functions of different tables, or of a class function and a list that is not a class function, is not defined and signals an error. Note: the product of values lists (plain lists) is the standard scalar product, so be mindful of type differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertibility of class functions without zeros
rubrics_metrics.description: Class functions without zero values are invertible; the inverse is defined pointwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such invertible class functions allow forming groups of linear characters, demonstrated by examples where pointwise division yields a Character.

rubrics_metrics.name: List-of-class-functions arithmetic semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of a class function with a list of class functions is the list of pointwise products (not a vector-matrix product). The product of two lists of class functions is the sum of the pointwise products (not the matrix product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when expecting matrix-like linear algebra operations on lists of class functions; use List/Map or convert to ordinary matrices (e.g., List(Irr, ValuesOfClassFunction)) if you need matrix inverse etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power operator ^ semantics for class functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The power operator ^ has several meanings: power by a nonnegative integer = tensor power; power by an element normalizing the underlying group or by a Galois automorphism = conjugate class function; power by a group or a character table = the induced class function; powering a group element by a class function = class function value at that element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ^ is overloaded, use explicit functions (e.g., Permuted) when appropriate; examples show chi^3, chi^(1,2), chi^g, and (1,2,3)^lin[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic of class functions and underlying characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic of class functions is zero, as for all lists of cyclotomics. For class functions of a p-modular character table, the prime p is given by the UnderlyingCharacteristic value of the character table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find the modular characteristic for Brauer characters, inspect UnderlyingCharacterTable and its UnderlyingCharacteristic attribute; Characteristic(irr) returns 0 for cyclotomic lists but underlying table reveals modular p.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplexConjugate / GaloisCyc / Permuted preserve class function status
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations ComplexConjugate, GaloisCyc, and Permuted return a class function when called with a class function; the complex conjugate of a (virtual) character is again a (virtual) character, and applying a Galois automorphism to an ordinary (virtual) character yields a (virtual) character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations preserve the known character/virtual-character property and the underlying table. Examples include ComplexConjugate(lin[2]) and GaloisCyc(lin[2],5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order semantics for class functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(chi) uses the general Order definition for monoid elements; the determinantal order of a character is the multiplicative order of Determinant(chi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute determinant character via DeterminantOfCharacter and then Order to get the multiplicative order of that determinant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing and display behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: ViewObj prints one of the strings "ClassFunction", "VirtualCharacter", "Character" (depending on known status), followed by ViewObj output for the underlying character table and the list of values. PrintObj behaves similarly but uses Print for the table; Display calls Display for the underlying table with chi as the only entry in chars list of the options record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the table (not the group) is shown, printing distinguishes underlying characteristics. To reduce printed space, give a name to the underlying character table via Name.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassFunction / VirtualCharacter / Character constructors do not validate values
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassFunction(tbl, values) returns the class function of tbl with given values. VirtualCharacter(tbl, values) and Character(tbl, values) return a virtual character or character respectively with values given, but it is not checked whether the given values really describe a virtual character/character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing characters from raw data, be aware that Character/VirtualCharacter do not validate; use IsCharacter/IsVirtualCharacter to check afterwards if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassFunctionSameType preserves known type information
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassFunctionSameType(tbl, chi, values) returns the class function ψ of tbl constructed with values; if chi is known to be a (virtual) character then ψ is also known to be a (virtual) character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ClassFunctionSameType when you want the constructed object to inherit character/virtual-character metadata from another class function object.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialCharacter / NaturalCharacter / PermutationCharacter semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: TrivialCharacter(tbl or G) returns the trivial character with value 1 on each class. NaturalCharacter(G) returns natural permutation/matrix representation character depending on group type; PermutationCharacter(G, U) returns permutation character for action on right cosets of subgroup U or given action domain and operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NaturalCharacter as a shortcut for permutation characters of transitive actions on cosets of a point stabilizer. PermutationCharacter has additional facilities for transitivity tests and computing possible permutation characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted/Induced class functions require class fusion information
rubrics_metrics.description: For restricting a class function of a group G to a subgroup H and for inducing a class function of H to G, the class fusion from H to G must be known (see 73.3). If necessary information is not uniquely determined by library tables then an error is signalled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tables from the library are used (without group access), many fusions and power maps are stored and can be used; otherwise you may need to specify an explicit fusion map or homomorphism. For factor groups, inflation requires either the natural homomorphism or the factor fusion stored on the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedClassFunction / RestrictedClassFunctions tbl-argument rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In function descriptions the optional first argument tbl is needed only if chi is a plain list and not a class function object; in this case tbl must be the character table of which chi shall be regarded as a class function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you pass plain lists instead of class function objects, always supply the relevant tbl argument to avoid ambiguity or errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: ScalarProduct definition and tbl requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ScalarProduct([tbl,] chi, psi) returns the scalar product of class functions chi and psi which belong to the same character table tbl. For ordinary class functions χ,ψ the scalar product is (∑g∈G χ(g)ψ(g−1))/|G|; for p-modular class functions the sum is over p-regular elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chi and/or psi are plain lists, provide tbl. The p-modular scalar product uses only p-regular elements; be careful when working modularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: MatScalarProducts behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: MatScalarProducts([tbl,] list[, list2]) returns the matrix of scalar products of entries of list with list2; if only one list is given a lower triangular matrix of scalar products is returned where row i contains scalar products with list[j] for j ≤ i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for computing decomposition matrices or multiplicities; supply tbl when lists are plain lists rather than class function objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm via decomposition into irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ordinary class function chi = ∑χ∈Irr(G) aχ χ, the norm of chi is ∑χ∈Irr(G) aχ aχ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute Norm to get squared length in the irreducible basis. Examples show using Norm on various characters and MatScalarProducts to inspect norms for sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConstituentsOfCharacter returns irreducible constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: ConstituentsOfCharacter([tbl,] chi) returns the set of those irreducible characters that occur in the decomposition of chi with nonzero coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works for ordinary and modular virtual characters; if chi is a list, specify tbl.

rubrics_metrics.name: KernelOfCharacter and ClassPositionsOfKernel semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: KernelOfCharacter([tbl,] chi) returns the normal subgroup of G formed by those conjugacy classes for which the value of chi equals the degree of chi. If the underlying character table does not store the group G then an error is signalled. ClassPositionsOfKernel returns the positions of those conjugacy classes (the implicit alternative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot access the group via the table, use ClassPositionsOfKernel to work implicitly with kernel positions to avoid errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CentreOfCharacter and ClassPositionsOfCentre semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: CentreOfCharacter([tbl,] chi) returns the centre of chi: the normal subgroup of all elements for which chi(g)/chi(1) is a root of unity. If the table doesn't store the group an error is signalled; ClassPositionsOfCentre returns positions as an alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use position-based functions when group objects are not available in table-only contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: InertiaSubgroup behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: InertiaSubgroup([tbl,] G, chi) returns the stabilizer in G of chi with respect to conjugation action (i.e., the set of g ∈ G with chi^g = chi), where chi is a character of a normal subgroup H of G. If tbl is omitted the underlying character table of chi is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires H normal in G and appropriate table/homomorphism info when chi is a plain list. InertiaSubgroup cannot in general be computed from character tables alone for non-normal subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation-character-specific tools (CycleStructureClass, IsTransitive, Transitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: CycleStructureClass([tbl,] chi, class) returns cycle structures for elements of a conjugacy class for a permutation character; IsTransitive([tbl,] chi) returns true iff the action is transitive; Transitivity([tbl,] chi) returns the maximal k such that the action is k-transitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions operate on permutation characters; supply tbl if chi is a plain list. Use NaturalCharacter when appropriate for coset actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CentralCharacter definition
rubrics_metrics.description: CentralCharacter([tbl,] chi) returns the central character ωχ defined by ωχ(g) = |g^G| · χ(g)/χ(1) for each g ∈ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CentralCharacter returns a class function (and may be used in further computations like restriction).

rubrics_metrics.name: DeterminantOfCharacter and eigenvalue tools
rubrics_metrics.description: DeterminantOfCharacter([tbl,] chi) returns the determinant character obtained by taking determinants of representing matrices of any representation affording chi; determinant can be computed using EigenvaluesChar. The determinant character is well-defined for virtual characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EigenvaluesChar([tbl,] chi, class) returns multiplicities of E(n)^k eigenvalues for representatives of given class; use these to compute DeterminantOfCharacter when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensored and TensorProduct convenience semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tensored(chars1, chars2) returns tensor products of all entries in chars1 with all entries in chars2 (chars may be values lists or class functions of same table). TensorProduct(chi, psi) returns the character afforded by the tensor product of modules and can also be computed as chi * psi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure both lists/characters refer to the same underlying table; Tensored returns a list of Characters/ClassFunctions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviour when underlying group is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a class function's underlying character table does not store the group G then operations that require the group (e.g., KernelOfCharacter, CentreOfCharacter) will signal an error; in such cases position-based alternatives (ClassPositionsOfKernel, ClassPositionsOfCentre) should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with library character tables that do not have associated groups, prefer functions and workflows that operate on class positions and stored fusions/power maps; specify explicit fusion maps when necessary.
